citations.label: Latent Programming Horizons in Coding Agents (arXiv)
citations.excerpt: a logistic-regression probe on hidden states is able to decode whether the current code parses, passes its test suite, reduces the number of failing tests, and introduces regressions, reaching AUC up to 0.83 for correctness across two models and two benchmarks

citations.label: Latent Programming Horizons, latent horizon finding
citations.excerpt: Probes trained to predict the outcome of future edits (before they are materialized and written on disk) achieve performance above chance up to roughly 25 steps in advance. We call this the agent's latent programming horizon.

citations.label: Latent Programming Horizons, transfer result
citations.excerpt: As a proof of external validity, we show that the probes transfer across benchmarks without retraining.

citations.label: Doomed from the Start, probe timing (arXiv)
citations.excerpt: Lightweight linear probes on internal activations predict eventual task failure from the first interaction round, substantially earlier than agent-monitoring methods based only on observable behavior.

citations.label: Doomed from the Start, token savings
citations.excerpt: The strongest settings reduce generated tokens by 60.2% on TextCraft and 54.9% on WebShop at 90% recall, while retaining savings of 45.0% and 41.5% at 95% recall.

citations.label: Doomed from the Start, behaviour-only comparison
citations.excerpt: Behavior-only monitoring is consistently weaker, and adding behavioral features to hidden-state probes provides no further gain.

citations.label: Doomed from the Start, recall guarantee
citations.excerpt: This design ensures that eventually successful episodes survive all early-stopping gates at a user-specified global recall rate. After selection, the cascade is frozen and certified on independent data, providing an exact post-selection recall guarantee.

citations.label: Doomed from the Start, evaluation setup
citations.excerpt: We evaluate the method on TextCraft and WebShop with Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-3B, and Qwen3-1.7B.

citations.label: ActProbe, the white-box objection (arXiv)
citations.excerpt: Existing online failure detectors either require white-box access to policy internals or add runtime overhead through resampling and observation-side signals.

citations.label: ActProbe, action-space result
citations.excerpt: ActProbe raises alerts before failures become visually recognizable, improving the accuracy (F1)-timeliness Pareto frontier of failure detection by an average hypervolume gain of +12.7% over both internal- and external-feature baselines, with a +9.0% early-detection ROC-AUC lead on unseen tasks.
